items.title: 4 Wall Street Giants That Raised Their Dividends for Income Investors
items.summary: Four big banks keep lifting their payouts, yet each one hides a different threat to the next raise. One cut its dividend to a dime, and another sits on a capital cushion that is shrinking fast. Which check can retirees trust most?

items.title: SpaceX Falls 5%, Breaks Below IPO Price as Lenders Reportedly Balk at Musk’s Orbital AI Chip Plans; Rocket Lab Drops 3%, AST SpaceMobile Dips
items.summary: Lenders reportedly wanted to keep Elon Musk from launching the very chips securing his massive AI financing into orbit. Now bond buyers are demanding a steep premium, and the fallout is rattling SpaceX shareholders.

items.title: What SPDR Dow Jones Industrial Avg ETF (DIA) Bought: Goldman Leads on Nov. 18
items.summary: The fund added $536.8 million in new buying across 29 positions, led by a $57.0 million purchase of Goldman Sachs.

items.title: Could Alibaba Actually Climb 112%? Or Is Goldman Sachs Totally Wrong?
items.summary: Key TakeawaysGoldman Sachs kept its Buy rating and $177 target on Alibaba after the Nov. 19 report, 112% above that day’s close and after a 53% fall from January’s high.

items.title: Goldman Sachs’ $177 Target Says Alibaba’s Selloff Went Too Far
items.summary: Key TakeawaysGoldman Sachs kept its Buy rating and $177 target on Alibaba into the Nov. 19 report, 112% above a stock 53% below its January high.

items.title: Anthropic’s Mega IPO Lives Up to Wall Street Hype but Fails to Revive AI Trade
items.summary: Investors remained wary of tech and AI stocks, as the Nasdaq composite resumed its recent slide, dropping 2.3% on Thursday.

items.title: Anthropic’s IPO nets Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley $113 million apiece in fees, eclipsing their SpaceX paydays
items.summary: The blockbuster public debut delivered one of Wall Street’s largest underwriting paydays in history.

items.title: Jim Cramer’s Warning for Anyone Buying Anthropic Stock: Use a Limit Order
items.summary: Anthropic opened far above its IPO price, then gave back a chunk of that gain within hours. Cramer says one small choice at the buy button separates smart entries from costly ones, and most retail buyers never see it coming.
